served.stem: Oligomycin plugs the proton channel of ATP synthase while leaving the electron transport complexes themselves untouched. What happens to the rate of electron flow through the chain?
choices: It increases, because protons are no longer being used up
It slows, because the gradient builds and pumping against it gets harder
It is unchanged, because the chain and ATP synthase work independently of each other
It slows, because oxygen can no longer accept electrons
It increases briefly and then stops as the matrix becomes acidic
served.bankWhy: This is respiratory control, and the gradient is the link between the two halves. With the synthase plugged, protons have no route back in, the gradient grows steeper, and the pumps eventually cannot push against it, so electron flow and oxygen consumption both fall. Contrast that with an uncoupler, which drains the gradient and makes the chain race.

answer.text: It slows, because the gradient builds and pumping against it gets harder
answer.line: The chain and ATP synthase are coupled through the gradient. Plug the synthase and the gradient backs up, so electron flow slows.

steps: Trace the protons. The chain pumps them out of the matrix, and ATP synthase is their main way back in.
Plug the synthase and protons pile up outside. The gradient gets steeper.
Pumping against a steeper gradient gets harder, so electron flow slows, and so does oxygen use.

choices.text: It increases, because protons are no longer being used up
choices.note: Speeding up is what an uncoupler does: it drains the gradient. A plug keeps the gradient full, which slows the pumps.

choices.text: It slows, because the gradient builds and pumping against it gets harder
choices.note: The gradient couples the two halves.

choices.text: It is unchanged, because the chain and ATP synthase work independently of each other
choices.note: It reads complexes untouched and stops there. The two halves are coupled through the gradient, which is the point of oxidative phosphorylation.

choices.text: It slows, because oxygen can no longer accept electrons
choices.note: It does slow, but that reason belongs to a complex IV poison such as cyanide. Oxygen is still there; the block sits at the synthase.

choices.text: It increases briefly and then stops as the matrix becomes acidic
choices.note: Protons are pumped out of the matrix, so the matrix grows less acidic, not more. And nothing here speeds up.
